content.title: What Is Pickleball | USA Pickleball
content.text: Pickleball is a paddle sport blending tennis, badminton, and table tennis, played indoors or outdoors on a badminton-sized court with a slightly lower net. Players use a solid paddle and a perforated plastic ball in singles or doubles, with underhand serves and the unique kitchen zone that encourages long, strategic rallies. As the sport’s National Governing Body, USA Pickleball sets official rules, approves equipment, sanctions tournaments, and supports programs nationwide. Easy to learn but challenging to master, pickleball is accessible to all ages and abilities, offering both casual fun and competitive play.History of PickleballBorn in 1965 on Bainbridge Island, Washington, pickleball began when three dads Joel Pritchard, Bill Bell, and Barney McCallum decided to entertain their bored kids with a unique new game using ping-pong paddles, a wiffle ball, and a lowered badminton net. The result? A sport that’s popular, endlessly fun, and full of heart.The BasicsLearn the basic rules and concepts for playing pickleball. Pickleball is a sport for everyone and learning to play is easy and fun.Court & LayoutA pickleball court measures 20 feet wide by 44 feet long for singles and doubles. The net is 36 inches high at the sidelines and 34 in the center. Each side has a 7-foot non-volley zone (“the Kitchen”), adding strategy and placement to play.EquipmentPlayers use a paddle made of rigid, non-compressible material, and a plastic ball with 26–40 circular holes. Both paddles and balls must meet official USA Pickleball specifications to be approved for tournament play. Pickleball can be played indoors or outdoors, with slightly different ball designs for each surface.Gameplay EssentialsEach rally starts with an underhand serve below the waist, hit diagonally. The Two-Bounce Rule requires the ball to bounce once per side before volleys. Only servers can score, games go to 11 (win by 2), and the non-volley zone promotes longer, more strategic rallies.Serving & ScoringOnly the serving side can score points. The server continues serving until a fault is made, at which point the serve passes to the other team. Most games are played to 11 points, win by 2, though tournament formats may extend to 15 or 21 points.The Two-Bounce RuleA defining feature of pickleball is the Two-Bounce Rule: after the serve, the ball must bounce once on each side of the court before volleys are allowed. This simple rule reduces the advantage of powerful serves and encourages longer, more exciting rallies for players of all levels.How to Play PickleballReady to start playing pickleball but not sure how? You can play singles or doubles, and rallies begin with an underhand serve across the court. Each side must let the ball bounce once before volleys. The Kitchen, a no-volley zone near the net, keeps rallies strategic. Only the serving team scores, and games are usually to 11, win by 2. Simple rules make for fast, fun, and competitive play at any level.Why People Love PickleballSuper Easy to Pick UpWithin minutes or a single short session, beginners often grasp enough to play and have fun.All Ages, All Levels Whether young or old, casual or competitive, pickleball is built to include, not exclude.Low Impact, High FunPickleball offers a great cardio workout with less strain, plus benefits for coordination, reflexes, and social connection.Friendly & Social CulturePickleball’s welcoming scene turns courts into communities making it easy to find partners, mentors, or lifelong friends.Where to PlayPickleball courts are popping up everywhere from public parks and rec centers to dedicated facilities. All you need to get started is a paddle and a ball. Looking for a place to play? Use our Find a Club or pickleball court locator tool to discover venues near you. For guidance on picking your first equipment, or choosing certified paddles and balls, check out our equipment pages.A Sport for EveryonePickleball is for everyone, from beginners to pros. USA Pickleball’s Skill Level scale makes it easy to find the right fit, grow your skills, and play with confidence. Discover your level and get started.Pickleball Community and CulturePickleball isn’t just a sport – it’s a community where everyone belongs. USA Pickleball, the National Governing Body, helps it grow through programs like USA Pickleball Serves, which provides courts and gear, as well as clinics for new players. We also sanction tournaments, certify referees, and support ambassadors who spark local play. Whether you’re here for fun, fitness, or competition, there’s a place for you on the court.
